A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreamBridge and contain readable main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite appendix reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original streaming, offline-video, and proactive-response evaluations, plus compression, training-data, latency, and activation-threshold analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds an accuracy ablation over memory budgets in Table 6.

M1.justification: The memory buffer, round-decayed compression, activation model, training supervision, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Compression code moves from Appendix G to I unchanged. New Algorithm 2 documents existing dataset construction rather than establishing a revised method, although its selection rule is ambiguous as noted under D1.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated tasks remain unchanged, including the full appendix benchmark coverage. The new memory-budget study reuses OVO-Bench and VideoMME; it adds model configurations rather than new datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main experiments, compression comparison, and full appendix results. Newly discussed ReKV and VideoStreaming are not added to the reported evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds an accuracy-evaluation sweep using Qwen2-VL-StreamBridge at 1 FPS with MaxLen values of 4k, 8k, 16k, and 32k. Existing benchmark protocols and the default 16384-token budget are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests how memory capacity affects streaming and offline accuracy, extending v1's memory-budget latency analysis. Existing compression-strategy, training-data, and activation-threshold ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new memory-budget table continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 6 newly reports OVO-Bench/VideoMME accuracy pairs of 70.49/61.7 at 4k, 70.89/63.6 at 8k, and 71.16/64.7 at 32k. Its 16k values, 71.30/64.4, match existing results. Previously reported tables and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Existing mathematical expressions and formal descriptions are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. The memory-budget interpretation is empirical, and Algorithm 2 adds procedural documentation rather than a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The introduction newly asserts that adaptation requires only minimal additional computation and data. The abstract, conclusion, and principal contributions concerning streaming adaptation, proactive responses, and preserved offline performance otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new MaxLen discussion interprets streaming accuracy as relying mainly on recent context, while offline tasks benefit from longer retained context. The limitations section removes v1's warnings about activation timing in complex scenes and insufficiently adaptive frame-level compression; synthetic-data shift and low-frame-rate limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds dataset-sequencing pseudocode as Algorithm 2. However, it selects the most similar next clip, whereas the retained prose describes sampling from a similarity distribution, leaving the intended implementation unclear. Existing hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix F adds ReKV and VideoStreaming references and expands discussion of the already cited StreamChat. It distinguishes their memory and retrieval approaches from StreamBridge's compression and proactive activation, without substantially redefining the overall positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose additions, adds Broader Impacts and More Related Works appendices, shortens limitations, and moves full benchmark results after limitations. Author contact information and conference text also change; most prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MaxLen table and dataset-construction algorithm display, resizes Figure 3 and clarifies its training caption, and relocates appendix tables. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise retained, with limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The MaxLen ablation strengthens the justification for the existing memory budget, and Appendix F clarifies distinctions from relevant prior methods. These provide a limited overall gain, tempered by removal of two concrete limitations and the new pseudocode's inconsistency with the clip-sampling description. The central method and previously reported results remain unchanged.
